name: Bounded Confidence: does locality end polarization? (§4.3)
description: HK §4.3's unfigured claim: with small, overlapping neighborhoods, 'polarization … disappears'. The metric is the second-largest camp's share of agents after 2000 periods (0 at consensus, near 0.5 with two equal camps), for everyone, a Moore torus and a von Neumann torus (25 × 25). Measured (release, seeds 1–5, recorded 2026-09-25): everyone listening, 0.31, 0.40 and 0.46 at ε = 0.10, 0.15 and 0.20, then 0; on either lattice it reads near 0 (never above 0.06), but at 2000 periods lattice camps are still closing — opinions within a camp still differ by more than 10⁻⁶ — so the sweep under-reads them. Run to stability (the survey, capped at 20 000 periods), a second camp of a fifth appears in 7 of 20 Moore runs at ε = 0.15 and 2 of 20 von Neumann runs at ε = 0.2, and never otherwise for ε 0.1–0.3 — 9 of 200 lattice runs against 57 of 100 among everyone — so HK's claim largely holds.
